Conditioning on ⋂iℰi(ji)\bigcap_{i}\mathcal{E}_{i}^{(j_{i})}, each event a function of path ii only, preserves the product; an analysed unit has path law Qipath(⋅∣Ai,≤t,ℰi)Q^{\mathrm{path}}_{i}(\cdot\mid A_{i,\leq t},\mathcal{E}_{i}), and an excluded unit contributes the factor one. Its one-block conditionals are

Qi,t​(a∣ℰi,Ai,≤t)=Qi,t​(a)​Pr⁡(ℰi∣Ai,≤t,a)Pr⁡(ℰi∣Ai,≤t),Q_{i,t}(a\mid\mathcal{E}_{i},A_{i,\leq t})=\frac{Q_{i,t}(a)\,\Pr(\mathcal{E}_{i}\mid A_{i,\leq t},a)}{\Pr(\mathcal{E}_{i}\mid A_{i,\leq t})},

Index the emissions by 0,…,T−10,\dots,T-1, so that TT is the terminal clock after the last emission. Let HtH_{t} be the hidden state just before the emission at clock tt, and let MtM_{t} be the bit mask of which fixed templates still match the emitted prefix (two templates give four mask values). A transition branch jj from state ss at clock tt has destination dt​(s,j)d_{t}(s,j), emission bt​(s,j)b_{t}(s,j) and probability wt​(s,j)w_{t}(s,j), and updates the mask to m∧matcht​(bt​(s,j))m\land\mathrm{match}_{t}(b_{t}(s,j)); the eligibility event holds iff the final mask is zero. βt​(s,m)=∑jwt​(s,j)​βt+1​(dt​(s,j),m∧matcht​(bt​(s,j))).\beta_{t}(s,m)=\sum_{j}w_{t}(s,j)\,\beta_{t+1}\bigl(d_{t}(s,j),\,m\land\mathrm{match}_{t}(b_{t}(s,j))\bigr).

Once the mask is zero, β≡1\beta\equiv 1 and the ordinary kernel applies. The sampling transition is used only at states with positive β\beta; states with β=0\beta=0 have probability zero under the conditioned sampler.

B.5 Design limits (Proposition 4)

Parts (a) and (b).

The exact denominator includes the term Qi,t​(Ai,tF)​eT⁡(Ai,tF)Q_{i,t}(A^{F}_{i,t})\,e^{T(A^{F}_{i,t})}, so ei,tex≤1/Qi,t​(Ai,tF)e^{\mathrm{ex}}_{i,t}\leq 1/Q_{i,t}(A^{F}_{i,t}); a point-mass law gives e≡1e\equiv 1. If KK of the BB draws equal the observed block, the MC denominator contains at least (1+K)​eT⁡(Ai,tF)(1+K)\,e^{T(A^{F}_{i,t})}, so ei,tmc≤(B+1)/(1+K)e^{\mathrm{mc}}_{i,t}\leq(B+1)/(1+K), and given the commands K∼Binomial⁡(B,Qi,t​(Ai,tF))K\sim\mathrm{Binomial}(B,Q_{i,t}(A^{F}_{i,t})). Within a product component, log⁡E\log E is therefore at most the sum of the corresponding per-factor log bounds. An arithmetic average of components can reach 1/α1/\alpha only if some component does. Under any alternative the actions still follow the design law, so integrating this necessary event over coherent full command paths drawn from QQ (and, for MC, over independent draws) bounds the rejection probability. Because averaging models adds no design entropy, the same command-only bound applies to the model average; for the Monte Carlo form this presumes that the models share their candidate bags, and otherwise the maximum runs over models with their own collision counts. The MC ceiling differs from the exact one: for a fair bit with B=20B=20 and a matching-score ratio of 10610^{6}, the MC test rejects only when no draw matches, with probability 2−202^{-20}, while the exact-form ceiling at α=0.05\alpha=0.05 is zero. The exact-form ceiling therefore bounds exact e-values only; for a Monte Carlo analysis it is a comparator.

Part (c).

B.13 Numerical checks

Two theory reviews (Appendix E) recomputed by exact enumeration the exact values stated in Propositions 3 and 4, the regression cases of the specification (exact sizes of the naive and set-averaged products under mutual spillover, shared noise and a path graph; the design ceilings for Q⁡(ON)=0.01Q(\mathrm{ON})=0.01 and for a fair bit with B=20B=20), and the forward–backward recursion and exact sampler of Proposition 2(b); the values agreed with those of the frozen documents. The first review also recomputed the exposure-clock cases. Both checked the identity of Proposition 7, which has no frozen counterpart, on random arrays. For Propositions 8–12, scripts checked the inequalities on random finite designs, the 8/98/9 grid constant, the rank constants and a closed-loop toy, and the independent review added ten counterexamples (heavy tails, shrinking competitor mass, floors, residue classes, null paths, ties, cross-unit copying, spillover feedback, grid coverage and sampled denominators), each of which the final statements respect; these checks are not exhaustive. The scripts and their outputs are archived with their hashes (Table 16).

Appendix C Design laws

Every validity statement of the paper is conditional on a working design law. This appendix states each law exactly, reports how it was checked against the released command records, and lists what remains unverified. The defining documents were committed before the M4 registration; their hashes are in Appendix E.

C.1 ERK

Laws.

In each field the light program is a train of pulses whose inter-pulse intervals were randomized by the acquisition protocol. All working laws hold the first and last pulse and the leading and trailing zero-command periods at each field’s observed values. In fields with a rest of 241 minutes between pulses, the variants differ in how they treat it: V1 fixes the rest’s rank among the intervals; V2 inserts the rest after the first pulse at or beyond a threshold time taken from a stated range, sampling full arrangements uniformly by rejection; and V3, the law used for every primary analysis, shuffles the non-rest intervals before and after the rest separately. Fields without a rest reduce, under every variant, to a uniform permutation of the multiset of intervals. Counts of arrangements are counts of distinct paths, so repeated gap lengths are not double-counted. At an origin, the conditional sampler keeps the completed intervals, conditions on the time elapsed since the last pulse by rejecting a too-short ongoing gap, and returns the future pulse train. Fields run under a binary encoding policy are deterministic and contribute e≡1e\equiv 1.

Checks.

All field-by-variant combinations passed unconditional checks of multiset, rank and segment structure, and simulated combinations passed conditional checks of the future train at several origins. Before any outcome was used, each field’s observed interval sequence was compared with uniform permutations of its own non-rest multiset (10,000 permutations, fixed seed) on three statistics: the Spearman correlation of interval length with position, the number of runs up and down, and the lag-one autocorrelation of intervals. A field was to be flagged if any statistic had two-sided p<0.01/39p<0.01/39, a Bonferroni correction over thirteen fields and three statistics. No field was flagged; the smallest per-field p-value was 0.0288, and the Fisher-combined p-values were 0.2921, 0.5117 and 0.7157 for the three statistics. The same procedure gated the M5 field (§8.4).

What remains unverified.

The acquisition protocol’s finite list of interval values, the uniformity of its shuffle, the rule that triggers the rest and the treatment of the series’ edges and time budget were not established from released code. An exchangeability check cannot certify an exact randomization kernel; it can only fail to find evidence against the working law.

C.2 CcaS/CcaR

The source law.

The released acquisition code draws, for each lineage, a pair of bounds and a hidden integer that starts at the midpoint and moves up or down by one with equal probability, clipped at the bounds. For the first thirty-six steps the command is forced off while the hidden walk keeps evolving; afterwards the command is on whenever the hidden value is non-negative. The exact forward filter of this law matched an independent brute-force enumeration to rounding error.

The source law fails, and so does a fitted alternative.

Under goodness-of-fit criteria committed before any statistic was computed, which compare on- and off-run-length distributions and lag correlations of the released commands with simulations from the law, the source law was rejected: every one of the seven dates failed at least the off-run total-variation criterion. A fitted order-kk Markov model of the commands (K4) also failed the frozen gate on two dates, so no fitted kernel was admissible.

The working law D1 and when it was found.

A diagnostic recorded during that check showed that the released commands match the source law delayed by one step, consistent with a one-step shift introduced at data export. Under the delayed law (D1), the run-length total-variation distances were at most 0.01485 across dates and run types, against a frozen threshold of 0.02. The delay was not one of the candidates evaluated in advance, and its documentation does not overturn the rejection of the source law or establish the actual export transformation; D1 is therefore a working law, and every CcaS result in the paper is conditional on it. Its first numerical record is dated 2026-10-06, and the D1 implementation was committed the same day, both before the M4 registration on 2026-10-08; it was thus found after the first design-law check failed, but before any registered analysis.

Fixed templates and eligibility.

On each date, most lineages follow the random walk, but some repeat one of two fixed command templates; across dates, 2735 rows belong to 14 template groups. The templates were identified as the command paths duplicated more than ten times on a date, and frozen by hash before calibration. Template rows have zero design entropy and contribute e≡1e\equiv 1; the random-walk rows are tested under D1 conditioned on avoiding both templates of their date, computed exactly by the forward–backward recursion of Proposition 2(b). That conditioning is exact only if the templates are genuinely fixed designs; because they were inferred from released duplicates rather than released by the experimenters, this is an assumption.

Neighbour exposure.

The released neighbour-exposure covariate is aligned one step ahead of the neighbours’ commands and would let a score use other lineages’ future actions. Every CcaS score uses its lag instead (§2.3); the sensitivity analysis restricted to lineages whose lagged exposure could be verified from commands is reported in §8.2.

C.3 Status of the working laws

Proposition 5 would bound the cost of a wrong working law if the law had been fixed independently of the tested commands and its distance from the true law were known. Neither holds here: the fitted law was estimated from the released commands, and D1 was chosen after the source law failed. We therefore claim no theorem-level guarantee for the working laws and rely on calibration with the released command records (§5.2), which bounds size empirically under the commands that were actually issued.

    Status line of the M5 plan. The registered plan is byte-identical to the file committed before the registration, whose header still reads that it is a draft and not registered. Its registered status is established by the OSF record and by the registration addendum, which states that it supplements the byte-identical plan (Appendix E).

  3. 3.

    Name of the M4 operational plan. The frozen specification refers to the operational plan as M4_ANALYSIS_PLAN_FINAL.md; the registered, hash-bound plan is M4_ANALYSIS_PLAN_v6.md, and the registration’s summary field stated this correspondence at registration. An older file named M4_ANALYSIS_PLAN_FINAL.md exists with different content and is a superseded predecessor.

  4. 4.

D.3 Disclosures by stage

Before M4.

M4 is a registered re-analysis of data analyzed earlier in BioWM-Eval (Appendix A), not a blind test. During the power pilot, a documentation search incidentally displayed earlier aggregate results; no setting changed on that basis. The designer of the sealed challenge had seen the source of the reference models and one correction to the challenge design. The CcaS working law D1 was adopted after the source law failed its goodness-of-fit check, before the registration (Appendix C); every CcaS rejection is conditional on it. The own-channel eligibility bound is vacuous. Observation-process assumptions (finite masks, segmentation) are stated, not tested. Power is low for weak or masked effects, and the e-value tests are conservative. The variance floor of the published CcaS model was active. The pilot gave each synthetic ERK field one trajectory, and the end-to-end rehearsal used a simple generator; neither could reveal pooling amplification.

M4 and its aftermath.

The M4 registration was submitted, and its content fixed, before any outcome was opened. OSF’s activity log for the associated project, public since the embargoes were lifted, records its approval about two days after submission, after the M4 training and test outcomes had been accessed (Table 13); the log does not show whether the approval was given by hand or by OSF’s automatic approval, which falls due 48 hours after submission. Until approval the registration could have been cancelled; it was not, and its content is fixed by the hashes in Table 12. Neither ERK positive control was rejected in the registered analysis. The diagnosis of pooling amplification, the selection of the repair and the exploratory analysis X all followed that failure; X was run on test fields opened in M4. The dated note that fixes interpretation rules for the positive controls was written after the M4 report had been read, and its rules only restrict claims. Two operational scripts (a launcher and a report formatter) were added during the test stage and are not in the freeze manifest; their hashes are in Appendix E. M4 did not save per-field, per-factor records, so the decomposition of its log e-values by field is not available. The repaired statistic’s correlation parameter was estimated on training fields only.

M5.

The M5 registration followed X; the plan had been committed before X and was not changed afterwards, and the registration disclosed the X results. The confirmatory field’s thirty-minute intervals lie outside the ten-to-twenty-five-minute training range. The single-field rehearsal used the linear-Gaussian model only. The command-law gate inherited the multi-field threshold of M1, which is lenient for one field. Permission to retry the data download was added in the execution instruction and implemented in a separate input–output adapter; it was not used. Origins at which every cell was masked were not tallied separately. The acquisition law of the confirmatory field is unverified, so validity is conditional on V3. OSF’s activity log records the approval of the M5 registration minutes after its submission and before the first data access (Table 14); a self-reported browser visit shortly after the logged approval is also archived. Five preparation files carry modification times later than X but are byte-identical to their earlier commits.

Pixel demonstration.

All results are simulated, from one simulator family and two model classes, with one training run per cell and a reduced compute budget. Kish tempering, registered for M5, did not repair pooling amplification there; contrast tempering, which restored power at the larger effect size, is exploratory and has no confirmatory test. Two expectations of the protocol were wrong: the oracle did not collapse under gain noise, and the fitted models also collapsed under offset noise. The trap experiment could not show the diagnostics’ growing confidence with data, and its frozen negative control was uninformative; the informative negative control was added post hoc. Three dated deviation notes record a reclassified pre-freeze audit flag (blocked standard-library probes, no data access), a reconstructed counter in the negative-control code, and a refresh of version-control index metadata in another repository.

ERK training diagnostic.

Command records were copied and hashed before the access marker was created; they are design information, not outcomes. The access log merges internal hash reads into logical open events, and the new repository’s version-control identity was read from an existing repository with non-modifying commands. The agreement between the two tempering factors is partly structural (Proposition 7).

Reviews.

The theory of §4 and Appendix B was checked in two AI-assisted review sessions with read-only access to the project, distinct from the drafting sessions and from each other: the first by Claude Code, the same model family as the drafting model, and the second by Codex, a different model family. According to the project records, the frozen theory documents had themselves been written in an earlier Codex session, so neither review is independent of all the authorship involved in the way a human statistician’s would be. Every bibliography entry was checked in a separate Claude Code session, which retrieved each source and checked each attributed claim against its text. Both theory reviews recomputed the stated exact values by enumeration. Neither found an error in the frozen proofs under their stated premises, and the bibliography review found no nonexistent reference. Both theory reviews found statements in our drafts that were stronger than what had been proved; the second also found that the hypotheses added to Proposition 6 after the first review did not exclude a predictor window that reveals the stratum. The revised text narrows these statements; the review archives record each finding and how it was addressed (Table 16). For this version, Propositions 8–12, which were drafted by Claude, and every sentence that uses them were checked by Codex in five further read-only sessions: an independent review with ten runnable counterexamples, a delta review of the revised draft, a check of the trap experiment’s logging policy against Proposition 12(b), a final check of the integrated text, and a delta check of its revisions. The final check also found that the duplicate-score rule of the baseline study does not by itself establish the exchangeability that the rank statistics need (Appendix H). The references added in this version were verified twice, in the drafting session and in a separate Claude Code session. The reviews check mathematics and citations; they do not certify the actual acquisition laws, the implementation of every named statistic, or the chronology of the archives.

Appendix H Baseline study

This appendix documents the exploratory baseline study of §6.4. It used only simulated data and the saved artifacts of the pixel demonstration and of the selection grid of §6.2; no real data were copied, opened or used. It was not registered on OSF. Its protocol, with the statistics, the decision rules and six dated predictions, was committed to the study’s repository with its hash recorded before any value of a new statistic was computed. Table 28 lists the commits and hashes of the protocol, its amendment and every result record cited below.

H.1 Protocol

Statistics.

The study added five statistics to those of the original runs: the rank e-values R and R1/2, the tempering mixture M over the grid λg=2−g\lambda_{g}=2^{-g}, g=0,…,12g=0,\dots,12, validation-tuned tempering V (§3.5), and ORACLE_R, the rank e-value of the oracle’s pooled score, as a reference for what a rank statistic can reach. V was set for each cell and learned model from the ten validation episodes and the validation bags of 3131 draws per origin that the contrast factor uses; every selected factor was written to a per-cell file whose hash was logged before any test score was computed. V is not defined on the ERK-like grid, which has no contrast design. Every statistic, old and new, was computed on the same test episodes and the same Monte Carlo draws (B=127B=127).

Ties.

In the pixel world the scores of the candidate blocks are computed in batched floating-point arithmetic, so identical action blocks in different columns of a bag can receive scores that differ in the last bits. For the rank statistics each column’s score was therefore replaced, before ranking, by the score of the first column with the same action block; distinct blocks were tied only when those scores were exactly equal, and the factor averaged gg over tied positions. This makes the scores of duplicate blocks identical within a bag. Exact mean-one validity additionally requires the scored bag to be exchangeable under relabelling of the candidates, and the first-occurrence rule alone does not establish that when numerical errors depend on a candidate’s position; we did not verify it for this run. The registered study of §9 computed one score per distinct action and does not rely on this rule. M and V use the scores unchanged, as contrast tempering does. On the ERK-like grid identical blocks already share one score.

Scenarios.

In the pixel world the study used the main grid of the demonstration: 2424 alternative cells with 1616 test episodes each and 1212 null cells with 3232, one episode being one decision unit, with rejection at E≥20E\geq 20 for the two-model average, as frozen. The trap grid of §7 was not part of the study. On the ERK-like grid it used the 1212 alternative cells with 1616 replicates each and the 22 null cells with 3232, one replicate being one decision unit, with the grid’s threshold E≥100E\geq 100.

Decision rules.

The primary comparison was the larger effect in the pixel world, 192192 decisions. A new statistic matched contrast tempering if its total rejections were at least the contrast-tempering total minus 1919 and it was at most 66 of 1616 below contrast tempering in every cell; it was clearly weaker if its total was at most the contrast-tempering total minus 4848, and intermediate otherwise. At the smaller effect a statistic was clearly stronger at 1919 or more rejections above contrast tempering and clearly weaker at 1010 or more below. On the ERK-like grid a statistic with two or more alternative cells below 1414 of 1616 was weaker than Kish tempering. A new statistic with two or more rejections in any null cell would have been stopped as a suspected implementation error. The protocol fixed, in order, four outcomes and what each would mean for this version of the paper: (1) R or M matches contrast tempering and is not weaker than Kish tempering on ERK-like data, in which case the repair is reframed around statistics robust to score magnitude and the better of R and M is recommended for new studies as an exploratory finding, its confirmatory use needing its own registration; (2) V matches but R and M are clearly weaker; (3) R, M and V are all clearly weaker; (4) anything else. In every case the role of Kish tempering in the registered analysis M5 was to stay unchanged.

H.2 Recomputation and the reproduction gate

The study reused the saved trained models, episodes and frozen parameters and reran only the test stage, and the validation scoring for V, on a different machine; nothing was retrained. Monte Carlo bags were regenerated from the frozen seed keys, and the convolutional model ran on a CPU with the frozen determinism settings. Before any new statistic was computed, a reproduction gate compared, for every test episode or replicate, the recomputed per-origin log factors and episode log⁡E\log E of every existing statistic with the saved records. A cell was EXACT if every difference was at most 10−9​max⁡(1,|x|)10^{-9}\max(1,|x|); CLOSE if it was not exact but every rejection decision was identical and the episode log⁡E\log E differences were small; and FAIL otherwise, which would have stopped the study.

The gate compared 51 cells, and in 51 of them every rejection decision was identical to the frozen record. As first written, the CLOSE tier bounded the relative difference of episode log⁡E\log E by 10−410^{-4}. That is ill-posed for reference values near zero, and 4 pixel cells were classified FAIL only because their references were close to zero. An amendment, written after these gate results and before any new statistic was computed, bounded instead the scaled difference |Δ|/max⁡(1,|log⁡Eref|)|\Delta|/\max(1,|\log E_{\mathrm{ref}}|) by 10−410^{-4}, the scaling the EXACT tier already used. It changed no statistic, grid, threshold or prediction. Under the amended rule 0 cells failed, and the largest scaled difference in any cell was 8.6×10−68.6\times 10^{-6}. The differences arose only in arms that involve the convolutional model. The amendment also recorded the tie rule above and a mechanical reading of the decision rules, before any rank value was computed; the gate records keep both classifications (Table 28).

H.3 Results

Table 29 gives the mechanical reading of the decision rules and the status of each dated prediction; Tables 30 and 31 give every cell. The rules returned outcome 1, and §6.4 follows the reading that the protocol attached to it. The prediction that R would match contrast tempering failed; §6.4 discusses a possible mechanism suggested by Proposition 11, whose baseline depends on tie handling and does not by itself explain the observed counts. The mixture became the primary statistic of the registered study of §9, which is the confirmatory test; this study is not.

Appendix I Registered test on a published world model

This appendix documents the registered study of §9: its registration and the order of events, the design in full, the two deviations and every result. Table 32 gives the identities, hashes and times on which the account rests; all times are UTC.

I.1 Registration and order of events

The protocol, its draft with the dated predictions, the pipeline and a pilot were committed to the study’s repository before registration. The confirmatory code was then frozen in one commit, after unit tests on toy inputs and an exact replay of the pilot, and the protocol, identified by its hash, and the frozen commit were registered on OSF (ctfxv). A note filed with the registration states that the dates written in the protocol text, including the date attached to the predictions, are labels assigned in advance, and that the authoritative times are the commit times and the registration time in Table 32; by those, the predictions were fixed in the draft protocol and carried unchanged into the registered version.

The confirmatory seeds could not exist before the registration. The protocol named a public randomness beacon, the drand mainnet chain of the League of Entropy (League of Entropy, 2026), whose rounds are scheduled every 3030 seconds, and the round used was the first scheduled at least 120120 seconds after the registration time. Every seed of the confirmatory run was derived by hashing a fixed label together with a master value, itself the hash of the protocol’s hash and the round’s randomness. The runner recorded the round’s signature and checked its format but did not verify it cryptographically; the record can be verified against the chain’s public key. Generation and analysis ran once from the frozen commit, behind a one-time marker with an access log, apart from the two restarts described in §I.3.

The pilot used separate seeds and never entered the confirmatory analysis. It ran the full pipeline on null units only (44 validation and 88 test units per game, 200200 steps), where the largest number of rejections by any statistic in any game was 0 of 88. On active pilot units it computed predictions, variances and the two estimated factors, but no e-value, rank, mixture, validation-tuned factor, p-value, rejection or replacement diagnostic.

I.2 Design

Model and emulator.

DIAMOND’s code was used at a fixed commit with its upstream files unchanged, and its released checkpoints for Boxing, Pong and Breakout at a fixed revision, with the hashes in Table 32. The model card states no licence for the weights; they were used for research inference only and are not redistributed. Only the denoiser was used, with DIAMOND’s three-step Euler sampler conditioned on the last four observations and actions. The emulator and preprocessing were those of DIAMOND’s training: the NoFrameskip-v4 environments of ALE 0.9.0 (Bellemare et al., 2013), sticky-action probability zero, four frames per action with the maximum of the last two, 64×6464\times 64 RGB frames by area interpolation, 11 to 3030 no-op actions at reset and the minimal action sets of 1818, 66 and 44 actions. Everything ran on one laptop GPU, in an environment whose exact specification is part of the frozen commit.

Units and eligibility.

A unit is one segment: one reset, then up to 500500 agent steps, ending earlier at the first termination or truncation. A life loss does not reset the emulator but makes the origins around it ineligible: an origin tt is eligible if the observations t−3,…,tt-3,\dots,t and the transition to t+1t+1 lie in one life. Each unit is tested on its own. A unit without eligible origins has E=1E=1 for every statistic and counts as a non-rejection; Table 33 lists such units.

Prediction and scores.

The candidate at origin tt is the label ata_{t}; the model conditions on the observations t−3,…,tt-3,\dots,t and on the recorded labels at−3,…,at−1a_{t-3},\dots,a_{t-1}, also in the NULL condition, and the target is the real observation Yt+1Y_{t+1} (h=1h=1, one residue class). The bag has 128128 columns: the recorded label and 127127 independent uniform draws. At each origin one Gaussian noise image was drawn and the model predicted once per distinct action in the bag, the validation contrast draws and the replacement draw, with that image; predictions were expanded back to the columns, so identical actions have identical predictions and scores. Predictions were stored as one of 256256 intensity levels, and a storage check stopped the run if a sampler output differed from its stored level by more than a set limit (§I.3). The per-site variance is the mean squared residual of the recorded-label prediction over all eligible origins of the validation units of the same game and condition, floored at (2/255)2(2/255)^{2}, and each site score is floored at log⁡10−12\log 10^{-12}.

Statistics.

The pooled score, the mixtures, the rank e-values and the rank tie rule are those of §3.5 and Appendix H, computed with the study code of the baseline study, copied byte for byte, and h=1h=1. Kish tempering uses the correlation estimate of §3.4 from the standardized validation residuals of the recorded-label prediction, clipped to [0,1][0,1]. Contrast tempering uses 3131 validation draws per origin and is clipped to [1/n,1][1/n,1]. Validation-tuned tempering maximizes the median validation log⁡E\log E over the 1616 validation units on the fifteen-value grid, ties going to the larger factor. The replacement diagnostic is, per unit, a one-sided one-sample t-test that replacing the recorded label by the replacement draw increases the mean squared prediction error, with an effect reported at p<0.05p<0.05; a unit with fewer than two origins or with all differences zero has no p-value and reports no effect.

Criteria, predictions and interpretation.

The criteria are those of §9.1. For validity the count governs; the accompanying one-sided Clopper–Pearson bound, written in the protocol as 0.0950.095, is 0.09512170.0951217 for 22 of 6464. The five dated predictions were: validity in all three games (95%95\%); collapse in at least two games (75%75\%); repair in at least two games (60%60\%); Kish tempering rejecting in fewer than 2424 of 3232 units in at least one game (60%60\%); and the rank e-value R rejecting less often than the mixture in at least two games (70%70\%). The protocol also fixed the interpretation: overall confirmation supports the claim that, on a published world model, pooling collapses the pooled test and the pre-specified mixture restores power while keeping validity; if collapse held but repair failed, the paper would say that tempering prevents collapse without guaranteeing power; and a validity failure would be treated as an implementation error, because validity holds by construction.

I.3 Deviations

Two integrity checks of the frozen code stopped the confirmatory run. Each was documented in a dated note, published on OSF before the run resumed (Table 32); neither changed generation, prediction, scoring, statistics, decision rules or gates, and both restarts reused the same beacon round and seeds.

Deviation 1: access log.

After the first unit, a null validation unit of Boxing, had been generated, stored and its hash verified, the runner’s check of the access log’s hash chain stopped the run. In two calls the unit’s file hash had been passed under the key that the log also uses for each row’s chain digest, so the digest overwrote it and could no longer be reproduced. No score or statistic had been computed for any confirmatory unit and no ACTIVE unit had been generated. The fix renamed the key, made the logging function refuse reserved keys, and added regression tests; the full test suite and the exact pilot replay passed. The aborted run was kept unchanged.

Deviation 2: storage tolerance.

The restarted run reproduced the first unit exactly and stopped after 84 completed units, in an ACTIVE validation unit of Boxing, because one sampler output differed from its stored intensity level by 2.66×10−72.66\times 10^{-7}, above the registered limit of two float32 epsilons. The sampler already rounds its output to an intensity level and returns it in float32, so the check measured float32 rounding only, while a level is unambiguous for any difference below 1/2551/255. The registered limit left too little margin: the largest difference in the pilot had been 2.05×10−72.05\times 10^{-7}, and this should have been noticed before registration. The limit became 10−510^{-5}, still far below half the spacing of the levels, so an output off the intensity lattice still stops the run; the change was one line, and no stored value changed. At this stop the runner had already analysed the Boxing NULL group, and ACTIVE validation units of Boxing had been generated; no ACTIVE test unit existed, and no score, e-value, rank, mixture, validation-tuned factor, p-value or rejection had been computed on any ACTIVE unit. The stopped run was kept unchanged.

Reruns.

The final run regenerated every unit of the stopped runs from the same seeds. Of 84 units compared array by array, 84 were identical, and the results of the Boxing NULL group were reproduced exactly.

I.4 Results

Table 33 gives every statistic in both conditions of each game, with the estimated and selected factors and the replacement diagnostic; Table 35 gives the criteria, the overall decision and the status of each prediction, as written by the analysis code. §9.2 summarizes them.

I.5 A post hoc illustration of the factors

The reading at the end of §9.2 rests on Table 36, a descriptive and post hoc calculation on a saved subset of the ACTIVE test units, the first four of each game, with no new simulation or sampling. For each unit the tempered log⁡E\log E was evaluated over the factors 2−k/42^{-k/4}, k=0,…,71k=0,\dots,71, with the saved observed-inclusive bags of 128128 scores, and the median of the four unit-wise maximizers is reported as the hindsight peak; this grid is used only here and is not a selection rule of the registered analysis. The margin column is the median across units of each unit’s median positive maximum competitor margin in its bags. In this subset the validation-selected factor lies near the hindsight peak and the contrast factor is an order of magnitude above it, with larger margin penalties, which is consistent with a possible pooling-amplification mechanism. By the bound (5), a sampled competitor of multiplicity kk limits the log factor by log⁡(128/k)\log(128/k) minus the tempered margin, so a positive margin alone does not make the factor negative. The calculation does not isolate a cause, does not test the unfloored identity of Proposition 9, and four units per game do not verify the counts of the full run.

J.2 Design details

The IRIS code revision was 24326aaaa283c527f42b89b44cfdecf2665a7a16, and its checkpoint revision was c0539e99adf924d44be0f19b12de00639daa5550. The TD-MPC2 code revision was 332f19e4aba4bffe2dc736f45ea7f7bdc585903a, and its checkpoint revision was 8fb2a82efb3bae96941da440128fe1332e4394fd. The MyoSuite wrapper patch, SHA-256 b9b09b337b02f2053beff2651c4398501bcdb9b95725e2d046b7f5d2ad598b51, removes the read-only Timeout assignment and passes the seed to the simulator constructor; it changes no dynamics or assets.

IRIS uses four emulator frames per action, 64 by 64 RGB frames resized with bilinear interpolation, and the maximum of the last two resized frames. Sticky actions are disabled, minimal action sets are used, and resets include 1–30 no-op actions. A life loss makes the affected origins ineligible without a pseudo-reset. An origin and its four-frame context must lie in one life. The token score is teacher-forced joint next-frame token likelihood over 16 tokens; the secondary decoded-pixel score uses the Gaussian over 12,288 sites in Boxing, Pong and Breakout. TD-MPC2 uses a Gaussian over 512 latent coordinates, with variances fixed on validation units and action repeat two for DeepMind Control Suite. Each unit ends at the first native termination, truncation or cap, retaining the terminal observation as its last target. The caps are 500 steps for the three DeepMind tasks, 100 for myo-pose and myo-reach, and 75 for myo-obj-hold.

Each condition uses 16 validation units, 32 test units under partial or full execution, and 64 under NULL. Bags have 127 design draws plus the observed action; validation contrast bags have 31 draws plus the observed action. Seeds are the first four big-endian bytes of the SHA-256 namespace consisting of the study identifier, phase, arm, task, condition, split, unit and stream. The confirmatory phase includes the master seed. PCG64 generates external non-noise streams; simulator reset seeds are passed to the frozen native simulator, and CUDA generators supply the pixel-sampling noise. Design draws are stored losslessly as float64 and converted to float32 at required model and simulator boundaries; identical converted inputs share predictions.

Validation units retain targets, observed-action predictions, the 31 contrast-draw predictions and replacement predictions. Test units retain all 128 bag-column scores in float64, the observed-action and replacement predictions, and targets. Other bag predictions are computed and scored but not stored; the token arm retains per-token target log probabilities of every distinct candidate. Decoded pixel means are clipped and rounded to nearest-even uint8, then dequantized by 2​k/255−12k/255-1 for scoring. Gaussian validation summaries are fixed before test generation. The protocol stores no model weights in its registration package.

J.3 Choice of the primary statistic

The regime map applied its pre-committed rule and selected V. The worst-cell rates were 0.8125 for V and 0.78125 for W(3/4), within the rule’s 1/32 tolerance; V won on mean rate. Amendment 1 left V and the weighted mixtures undefined for the saved ERK-like cells, because validation scores and residuals were missing. The later ERK validation-tuning check gave V a four-model log e-value of -101 at thirty minutes, with all four models negative, and two negative models at ten minutes; M gave 347 and 218 and W(3/4) gave 345 and 217. Protocol Section 2.1 registered W(3/4) before any confirmatory data existed. This departs from the regime map’s protocol, which said that its selection rule would fix the primary statistic.

J.7 Compute

The synchronized GPU-stage hours were 2.53421079 for IRIS tokens, 2.86836434 for the secondary decoded pixels, and 0.0810389767 for TD-MPC2. The secondary pixel units are shared with IRIS tokens and are not additional distinct units. Overall wall time was 8.27198099 hours. Other processes shared the GPU during the run; this affects timing only. GPU-event hours were not emitted by the frozen code.

Appendix K Exploratory studies after the second version

K.1 Score-rule study

The score-rule study was exploratory, under the protocol dated 7 November 2026, SHA-256 3e772433628581b0d600a80fdbdce4153b8f0f6b3f6bf36fe459bd2dcfce3c79. It rescored saved DIAMOND predictions, observations and bags without generating new units. The reproduction gate recovered all rejection decisions of the registered run before any alternative score rule. The ten alternatives were the two higher variance floors, one common variance, Student-t and Laplace densities, three block sizes, a 256-dimensional random projection and a rank-16-plus-diagonal joint Gaussian. Kish and contrast factors are undefined for the joint Gaussian. No scientific method deviation was recorded; an initial file-name discovery traversed broader directories, after which access was restricted to the authorized inputs.

K.2 Sampling study

The sampling study used the same protocol, with four predictions averaged at each eligible origin, and was exploratory. Its reproduction gate recovered the registered validation unit bit for bit, including all bag, contrast and replacement predictions. The initial disk rule stopped the study before generation. A dated amendment replaced it with a 100 GiB rule; the reproduction and 20-origin timing gates passed before generation. All 288 planned units completed. The saved readout records 12.925915 GPU-event hours and 13.08265 hours elapsed wall time. The two predictions dated 7 November 2026 were that collapse persists (probability 0.65) and that M repairs it where it persists (0.80); both were supported.

K.3 Regime map

The regime map was exploratory, under the protocol dated 8 November 2026, SHA-256 f9ab5aeed26592704b5a71b0daa6df7df826a00acdb64468daae241f4c078eeb, and Amendment 1, SHA-256 9ea8ec9b1d1566da23f7e3e78e55313f96b48f7db94f485bd9d671726847e983. The simulator and crossed grid are described in Section 6.5. Oracle-only calibration fixed the weak, medium and strong effects at 0.04296875, 0.078125 and 0.140625, targeting median log e-values of 3, 10 and 30 and attaining 3.23815054017, 10.328241766 and 30.9656204875. Calibration stopped within ten percent of target; its values were committed before the other new statistics were computed.

Amendment 1 followed the initial stop on missing ERK-like validation quantities. It leaves V, contrast tempering and W undefined on those cells; uses the 15-value mixture for selection while reproducing the baseline study’s native 13-value mixture in the gate; restricts decision-relevant cells to common defined candidates; and excludes candidates using only the simulator’s null cells. It fixes 31 validation draws and the calibration stopping rule. The restarted baseline reproduction gate passed on all 51 cells, with 10,824 comparisons, zero log-e-value differences and zero rejection mismatches. The baseline study’s pixel-world Kish factors and residual correlations were not saved; their existing C1 results were retained without back-calculating parameters.

Selection step 1 excluded no candidate: every simulator null maximum was zero. Step 2 gave the highest worst-cell rate, 0.8125, to V. Step 3 treated W(3/4), at 0.78125, as tied within 1/32; mean simulator rates 0.634837962963 and 0.625192901235 selected V. Step 4 was not needed. There were 98 common decision-relevant cells. Q2 found a paired median V-minus-M deficit of at least half log 15 in 28 of 54 weak-effect cells, a fraction of 0.518518518519.

The main driver stopped on an analytic-reference lookup after all other 230 cells were saved. The corrected reference handler used the saved per-replicate residual correlations, reused C0 when the Kish factor equalled one, and completed the reference statistics; all earlier outputs stayed unchanged. Exact total main CPU time was not captured. The original stop records were preserved.

K.4 ERK validation-tuning check

Protocol v1, dated 8 November 2026, SHA-256 f48d4ac7460886e104720e052d3b9d3cfb4b6c695a8616028082c161bce67e79, stopped because the frozen M4 assets were absent on the new machine. Version 2, SHA-256 baf5090abb2b4c4578056f42ba1efbee558f5d486229657335b5c9337985fb2d, ran on the old machine, defined validation bags and added weighted mixtures without changing the four predictions. The reproduction gate recomputed C0 at ten and thirty minutes within 0.01 of M4 and reproduced the rounded C1 values 349 and 218 from X.

The dated predictions and outcomes were: M reaches E at least 100 at both horizons (0.90), held; V does so (0.75), failed; R stays below 100 at ten minutes (0.65), failed; and M remains within log 15 of the best constant-grid member at both horizons (1.00), held. The gaps were 2.70805020020578 and 2.70802211364344, below log 15 = 2.70805020110221.

DEVIATION_01 changed a new accumulator from float32 to explicit float64, after the first attempt had passed the reproduction gate. The deviation and fix were committed before reopening. A formatting-only readout step later converted completed-table booleans to native JSON; it reopened no field and recomputed no score or statistic. The cumulative log records 52 ERK file opens: 26 trajectory-member opens and 26 command-snapshot opens, including both attempts. There were zero action-registry opens, zero historical outcome or score-cache reads and no refitting.

K.5 ERK field inventory

The ERK field inventory used archive metadata and the projects’ retained identity and access records, without opening a biological archive member. Declared TRAIN, TEST and M5 assignments were preserved. Remaining fields were classified OPENED-OR-UNKNOWN whenever their lifetime opening history was missing or ambiguous; absence of a matching record was not treated as proof of non-access. The result was 67 fields OPENED-OR-UNKNOWN and zero UNOPENED. During the inventory, a source preview showed at least one hard-coded historical ERK summary value; no outcome value was reproduced, and source previews were stopped. This does not affect M5, whose field was opened only under its registration.

K.6 Weighted mixture on DIAMOND (post hoc)

Not computed: the saved registered-run and sampling-study per-unit records contain final statistics and validation-grid values, but do not contain every test unit’s whole-unit e-values at all 15 grid values. The conditional computation was therefore not run. The corresponding DIAMOND cell in Table 7 is a dash.
